newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to give Jordan $100 million aid.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to give Jordan $100 million aid.

text.p: The United States announced Tuesday it was giving Jordan $100 million aid this year through a newly created Middle East peace and stability fund to reward Amman for its dedication to the peace process.
State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said the money would be raised by deducting $50 million each from current aid allocations to Israel and Egypt.

Secretary of State Madeleine Albright told a brief news conference that President Bill Clinton "is announcing today our intent to create the Middle East peace and stability fund". She gave no figures but Burns later supplied financial details.

The purpose of the fund, approved by Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, "will be to assist Jordan as it moves forward on the path of economic development," Albright said.

"The creation of this fund shows our support for King Hussein's leadership and for the people of Jordan as they embrace democracy and as their nation remains at the forefront of efforts with Israel and other friends of peace to enhance regional cooperation and stability."
The United States has been worried that popular support in Jordan for the struggling Middle East peace process could wane still further unless its people received tangible benefits.
